title: Interior design studio opens a home decor shop at the Chadds Ford Barn Shops
summary: The Shop at Punctuate Your Style has relocated to 1609 Baltimore Pike, Suite 400, selling home decor, gifts and seasonal pieces alongside owner Ashley Dowse's design practice. A grand opening with food, wine and live music runs Saturday, Oct. 17, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

title: About 100 West Brandywine residents push back on a 237-home Toll Brothers plan
summary: The builder wants conditional-use approval for an age-restricted community on 116 acres between Hibernia and Manor roads, a site neighbors say is too far from a hospital and already surrounded by three other 55-plus projects. Three hearings are done and the township expects about three more before supervisors vote.
loc: Hibernia Rd & Manor Rd, West Brandywine (near Coatesville)

title: Health officials flag a Kennett Square CVS in the county's growing measles outbreak
summary: Anyone at the CVS at 870 Baltimore Pike on Sunday, Oct. 4, between 10:45 a.m. and 3 p.m. may have been exposed, along with two West Grove stores the same afternoon. Chester County has logged 83 confirmed cases, and Oxford High School closed Friday after a case in its school community.

title: West Chester Chili Cook-Off moves to Sunday, Oct. 18
summary: Organizers postponed the Gay Street cook-off from Oct. 11 to its rain date because of the remnants of Hurricane Isaias, and all tickets bought for the original date remain valid. The event runs noon to 4 p.m. with 27 chilis, more than 60 vendors and live bands.

title: West Goshen asks a court to raze the burned-out former Boston Market
summary: The township has petitioned Chester County Court to appoint a conservator for 726 E. Gay St., which partially collapsed in a December 2024 fire and has racked up 54 open citations. The proposed plan demolishes the building and lists the lot for sale, with a hearing set for Nov. 2.

title: The Wardrobe reopens in Malvern after losing its Exton Square Mall space
summary: The nonprofit, which gives away free clothing and career coaching, held a ribbon cutting Thursday, Oct. 8, at the former Goodwill in Lincoln Court Shopping Center. Donations are accepted Tuesdays and Thursdays from noon to 4 p.m., and the group expects to serve a record 2,000 Chester County residents this year.

title: Century-old Hoffman's Mill dam comes out of the Brandywine in Chadds Ford
summary: The Brandywine Conservancy removed the breached low-head dam near the Route 1 bridge on Oct. 6, ending nearly six years of planning. The 2025 flood study flagged the remains as a debris trap, and the open channel now lets shad migrate and paddlers pass without a portage.
loc: Brandywine Creek at Route 1, Chadds Ford

title: Westtown weighs selling the 1823 Darlington Inn, and preservationists want its facade protected first
summary: The township carved the serpentine-stone inn out of the Crebilly Farm purchase to save it from demolition, but says it has no municipal use for the building and has rezoned it commercial. Founders of the new Westtown-Brandywine Historical Society are asking for an exterior easement before any sale, modeled on Painter's Folly in Chadds Ford.

title: West Chester Co-op cuts the ribbon on the borough's first grocery store in decades
summary: More than 100 member-owners turned out for the grand opening of the community-owned market on West Market Street, which had been in a soft launch since Aug. 20. The store is open to everyone, no membership required.

title: Downingtown's mother. closes a week after its first birthday; Willowdale venue opens in Kennett Square
summary: The upscale Mexican restaurant at 202 E. Lancaster Ave. served its last meals Saturday, Oct. 10. Across the county, Jeffrey A. Miller Hospitality's Willowdale events venue is now open on the former Landhope Farms dairy property after a yearlong overhaul.
